_comment: Router port-forwarding instructions. Adding a router is a pull request, not a release.
Every entry carries a 'source': the vendor page its menu path was checked against.
An entry without one has not been verified and should not be trusted over the generic
fallback. This field exists because the first version of this file was written from
memory and read exactly as confidently as a checked one.
Matching is tried in this order, most reliable first:
vendor  - substring of the manufacturer the router reports over UPnP. Most reliable.
banner  - substring of the gateway admin page title or Server header. Used when UPnP is off.
oui     - first three octets of the gateway MAC, lowercase colon-separated. Works when
the router answers nothing at all, but only identifies the vendor.
OUI lists are sparse on purpose: a wrong prefix produces confidently wrong instructions,
which is worse than the generic fallback. Only add prefixes you have verified on hardware.
Menu paths vary by firmware version. Keep 'note' for the step people actually get stuck on.
'upnpPath' is where automatic port opening is switched on, cited by its own 'upnpSource'.
It is optional, and it is the field most worth leaving blank when unsure: it is offered as a
way to skip the manual guide entirely, so a wrong path costs more than no path at all.

asus.name: ASUS
asus.upnpPath: Advanced Settings → WAN → Basic Config → Enable UPnP
asus.note: Switch 'Enable Port Forwarding' to ON before adding a rule. It is off by default, and the table will not accept rows until it is on. Then use 'Add profile'. Older ASUSWRT calls the page Virtual Server only, with the rules in a table on the page rather than behind Add profile.
asus.reservationPath: LAN → DHCP Server → Manually Assigned IP around the DHCP list

tplink.name: TP-Link
tplink.note: Depending on the model this is called 'Virtual Servers' or 'Port Forwarding'. Older firmware puts it under Forwarding → Virtual Servers instead, with no Advanced tab.
tplink.reservationPath: Advanced → Network → DHCP Server → Address Reservation

netgear.name: NETGEAR
netgear.path: ADVANCED → Advanced Setup → Port Forwarding / Port Triggering
netgear.upnpPath: ADVANCED → Advanced Setup → UPnP → Turn UPnP On
netgear.note: Choose 'Port Forwarding' rather than 'Port Triggering' — they are different features. Then use 'Add Custom Service' rather than picking from the service list. Older Smart Wizard firmware has no Advanced Setup level: it is simply Advanced → Port Forwarding / Port Triggering.
netgear.reservationPath: ADVANCED → Setup → LAN Setup → Address Reservation

fritzbox.name: FRITZ!Box
fritzbox.note: Port sharing is added per device: choose 'Add Device for Sharing', pick this computer, then add a sharing for the port below. Older FRITZ!OS releases label the same screen Port Forwarding rather than Port Sharing.
fritzbox.reservationPath: Home Network → Network → the device's Edit pencil → 'Always assign the same IPv4 address'

linksys.name: Linksys
linksys.path: Security → Apps and Gaming → Single Port Forwarding
linksys.note: On older classic-firmware routers, the WRT series among them, Applications & Gaming is a tab of its own along the top rather than sitting under Security. The Linksys app has the same thing under the router's settings.

ubiquiti.name: Ubiquiti UniFi
ubiquiti.note: UniFi has moved this twice. On Network 9.3 it is Settings → Policy Table → Create New Policy → Port Forwarding; on older releases, Settings → Firewall & Security → Port Forwarding, and older still, Settings → Routing & Firewall.
ubiquiti.reservationPath: Client Devices → the device → Settings → Fixed IP Address

mikrotik.name: MikroTik
mikrotik.path: IP → Firewall → NAT → add a dst-nat rule
mikrotik.note: Set chain to dstnat, protocol tcp, dst-port to the port below, then action=dst-nat with to-address and to-port set to the values below.
mikrotik.reservationPath: IP → DHCP Server → Leases → make the lease static

synology.name: Synology Router
synology.path: Network Center → Port Forwarding → Port Forwarding
synology.note: Port Forwarding does not appear at all when the router is in wireless access point or repeater mode.
synology.reservationPath: Network Center → Local Network → DHCP Clients, then add the device to the reservation list

verizon.name: Verizon (Fios)
verizon.note: The Advanced toggle is the step people miss: in the simple view there is no Port Forwarding entry at all. The rule asks for 'Original port' and 'Frwd to Port', which are both the port below, and a Schedule, which must be left on Always rather than User Defined. On an older Fios Quantum Gateway (G1100 or MI424WR) there is no Advanced toggle and it is simply Firewall → Port Forwarding along the top.
verizon.reservationPath: Advanced → Network Settings, in the DHCP settings for your network

eero.name: eero
eero.path: eero app → Settings → Network settings → Reservations & Port Forwarding
eero.note: eero requires the mobile app; there is no web admin page. The reservation and the forward are created together on this screen.
eero.reservationPath: the same screen — adding an IPv4 reservation is the first half of adding the forward

google.name: Google Nest Wifi
google.path: Google Home app → Home Wifi Settings → Advanced Networking → Port management → Add
google.note: Choose the IPv4 tab, then pick this computer from the device list before entering the ports. If you set the network up years ago you may still have the older, separate Google Wifi app, where the same screen is under Settings → Network & general → Advanced networking.

xfinity.name: Xfinity (Comcast)
xfinity.path: Xfinity app → WiFi → View WiFi equipment → Advanced Settings → Port Forwarding → Add Port Forward
xfinity.note: Choose Manual Setup rather than picking an application from the list. If Advanced Security is on and decides the port looks risky it will block it again afterwards, which looks exactly like the rule not working. An older, non-xFi Xfinity Gateway still has a web page at http://10.0.0.1 with Advanced → Port Forwarding → Add Service; on current xFi gateways only the app works.
xfinity.reservationPath: the same Advanced Settings screen — port forwarding only offers devices using IPv4 and DHCP

att.name: AT&T
att.note: You need the Device Access Code printed on the side of the gateway to change anything. Under Service, choose Custom Services to enter the port below rather than picking an application.
att.reservationPath: Settings → LAN → IP Address Allocation, by setting this computer's address to fixed

spectrum.name: Spectrum (Charter)
spectrum.path: My Spectrum app → Services → Network Equipment → your router → Advanced Settings
spectrum.note: The Add Port Assignment button stays greyed out until you have reserved this computer's address on the same screen. Reserve it first and the button turns blue.
spectrum.reservationPath: the same screen — open this computer under Create IP Reservations and turn on Reserve IP Address

bt.name: BT Hub
bt.path: the Hub Manager at http://192.168.1.254 → Advanced Settings → Firewall → Port Forwarding
bt.note: The admin password is on the settings card on the back of the Hub, not your BT account password. Use 'Create a new port forwarding rule', and put the same number in both the Start and End boxes.
bt.reservationPath: Advanced Settings → Home Network → IP Addresses, by giving this computer an always-use-this address

virginmedia.name: Virgin Media Hub
virginmedia.note: A TCP rule on port 443 does not take effect until the Hub is restarted, so restart it after saving or the rule will look like it did nothing. Fill in Local and External start and end ports with the same number.
virginmedia.reservationPath: Advanced Settings → DHCP, by reserving this computer's address

sky.name: Sky Hub
sky.path: My Sky app → Broadband → Product Settings → Advanced settings
sky.note: Sky moved these settings out of the hub's own pages and into the app for the Max Hub. On an older Sky Hub 4 or earlier they are still at http://192.168.0.1 under Advanced → Security → Services → Add Service.
sky.reservationPath: the same Advanced settings screen, where the device is selected before the ports

orange.name: Orange Livebox
orange.note: Orange calls port forwarding NAT/PAT. The rule will not accept this computer until it has a fixed address, so set that first in DHCP. Older Livebox 4 and 5 firmware put the same page under Configuration avancée.
orange.reservationPath: Paramètres avancés → Réseau → DHCP, by giving this computer a fixed address

freebox.name: Freebox
freebox.path: http://mafreebox.freebox.fr → Paramètres de la Freebox → Mode avancé → Redirections de ports
freebox.note: The same settings are in the Freebox Connect app under Réseau, and in your Espace Abonné under Mes équipements Freebox → Server internet → Paramètres réseau avancés.
freebox.reservationPath: the DHCP section of the same advanced settings, as a bail statique

telstra.name: Telstra Smart Modem
telstra.note: Depending on the model this is called WAN Services or just Services, and on some it sits under Advanced → Firewall instead.
telstra.reservationPath: the modem's DHCP settings, by giving this computer a fixed address

bell.name: Bell Home Hub
bell.path: http://192.168.2.1 → Advanced tools and settings → Port forwarding
bell.note: On Bell's wireless home internet, rather than fibre, the hub sits behind a second layer of NAT that you cannot configure, and no port forwarding rule will work. On fibre it does.
bell.reservationPath: Advanced tools and settings → DHCP, by reserving this computer's address

rogers.name: Rogers Ignite
rogers.path: Rogers Xfinity app → WiFi → View WiFi equipment → Advanced Settings → Port Forwarding → Add Port Forward
rogers.note: Rogers moved these settings into the app; the gateway's own pages no longer offer them. Give this computer a static address first or it will not appear in the device list.
rogers.reservationPath: the same Advanced Settings screen, under the device's details

_default.name: Your router
_default.path: the section called 'Port Forwarding', 'Virtual Server', 'NAT', or 'Applications & Gaming'
_default.note: Menu names vary between manufacturers and firmware versions.
_default.reservationPath: the DHCP settings, usually called 'Address Reservation' or 'Static Lease'
